Full year guidance is updated to include the impact of sports results and the previously disclosed impact of the Brazil closure, partially offset by mitigating cost actions. This results in a reduction in full year Group revenue midpoint guidance of $300m to $17.61bn, and a reduction in full year adjusted EBITDA guidance of $160m to $2.495bn. Dan Taylor, CEO, commented: “It is a privilege to take on the role of Flutter CEO. I know this business and the industry well, and I have a clear view of our strengths, where we need to improve, and where the biggest opportunities lie. Online betting and gaming is still a relatively young industry, with significant room to grow as markets develop and customer behavior evolves. Flutter enters its next phase from a position of strength. We have leading businesses in many of the world’s most attractive markets, great brands and scale advantages that few others can match. Our job now is to make more of those advantages. Our Q3 performance gives me confidence that we are moving in the right direction. In the US, our sportsbook improvement plan is delivering early but tangible progress in customer engagement and performance. Our International business continues to benefit from strong underlying momentum and the impact of our cost transformation programs. Looking ahead, our priorities are clear: build on our US leadership, capture the prediction markets opportunity, unlock more value from our International portfolio and simplify the way we operate. Delivering against those priorities will require faster execution, tough decisions and disciplined investment. I am confident our actions will make Flutter a stronger business in the long-term.” 2 To our shareholders, This is one of my first opportunities as CEO to set out my initial thoughts and priorities. Having worked at Flutter and in the industry for many years, I know the strengths of our business well, and also the improvements required to deliver our next phase of growth. Flutter is the largest online gambling business with number one positions in many of the world’s most attractive betting and gaming markets. We have fantastic brands, deep sector expertise and significant scale, but we are not getting enough from these advantages. We need to simplify how we operate and move faster, removing costs so that we can invest more behind the right opportunities with the strongest long-term returns. Our Q3 performance shows that the actions we have already taken are the right ones. Underlying performance in the US was ahead of expectations, while in International we are building on our transformation program and delivering market share gains in our core markets. Sports results went against us in the quarter, however, which is reflected in our updated 2026 guidance. Against that backdrop I have four immediate operational priorities: building on our US leadership position; capturing the prediction markets opportunity; driving more value from our International portfolio; and simplifying our operating model. Delivering on these priorities will require clear leadership and tough decisions, while remaining disciplined in our investments, focused on improving our cashflow conversion and deleveraging the balance sheet. Build on our US leadership position I strongly believe we have the best assets to capture the significant opportunity in the increasingly competitive North American market. However, we must reaffirm our US leadership position by operating at a faster pace, delivering relentless product innovation, and investing where we see the opportunity to deliver long-term value. We took decisive action earlier in the year to improve our value proposition and increase our share of wallet, including the launch of our FanDuel Rewards program and accelerating our product roadmap. These actions are delivering encouraging returns; our sportsbook performance was ahead of expectations and we took market share. Customers are responding well to these changes; generosity perception increased seven percentage points 8 , while player frequency rose 4%, and bet count grew 15% 9 . Sportsbook revenue increased 4%, reflecting promotional spend increasing to market levels, with strong AMP and handle growth of 9% and 13%, respectively. This good performance provides a solid base for us to build on. We must continue what we are doing well, while ensuring our customer proposition remains at competitive levels. I am confident we are making the right decisions to defend our leadership position and deliver FanDuel’s long-term success. We continue to see a limited impact from prediction markets on the betting activity of our existing customer base, which I believe, and our consumer research affirms, reflects the superior proposition offered by sportsbooks. We are, however, beginning to see an impact on our overall media costs as prediction market operators increase marketing spend. The duration of this trend will depend in part on how the regulatory landscape develops, but at this early stage, we expect our marketing intensity 10 to continue in 2027 at levels similar to this year. Over the last four years, we have transformed FanDuel Casino from a distant third place, into the market-leader 1 by delivering best-in-class content and rewards to our customers. We must ensure we maintain our laser-focus on our customer proposition, delivering market-leading content. Player engagement in Q3 was strong with AMP growth of 24%. Revenue growth moderated to 8% primarily driven by competitive dynamics, and market moderation as the US iGaming states move through the maturity curve. Looking forward, the potential for new states to regulate iGaming provides very significant upside, as evidenced by our very strong launch in Alberta in July. 3 Capturing the prediction markets opportunity Prediction markets represent a significant incremental growth area. Our priority is to build a strong position now, investing with discipline and maintaining flexibility to adapt quickly as regulation develops. We believe the actions we have taken in recent months mean we are much better positioned to deliver in three core areas: First, we must deliver a competitive product. The nationwide launch of our FanDuel One App and the transition of all sports contracts to Crypto.com, means we believe we now have a much more competitive sports offering that customers like and are increasingly engaging with. We have more work to do, and we have a clear plan to further strengthen our customer proposition. Second, we must use the strength of the FanDuel brand to acquire customers and build a meaningful database in non-sportsbook states. Initial trading volumes are encouraging with total October volume growth almost tripling when compared with July. The customers we are acquiring look like typical sportsbook customers, demonstrating similar characteristics, but with lower costs per acquisition. We are investing at a level that we believe will position us well for the long term, balancing the need to operate at scale in targeted states, against the regulatory uncertainty in this space. Third, we can use our leading expertise in pricing sports events, and in particular complex correlated events to drive market-making growth. We are making excellent progress, we are on track to deliver our guidance for 2026, and going forward we believe that this growth will help fund our prediction market customer acquisition spend. Unlock more value from our International portfolio We have built a portfolio of regional powerhouses with number one positions in many of the world’s major regulated markets. Our scale allows us to invest in better products and customer experiences, while we believe our diversified business delivers resilient growth when individual markets face regulatory or economic change. My focus is on consistent execution, sustained growth and further market share gains. We made good strategic progress during the quarter, strengthening our market-leading positions in Italy, UKI and CEE. Successful integrations in Italy (Snai), UKI (Sky Bet) and PokerStars are unlocking meaningful revenue upside, with cost benefits expected to be in excess of our $300m target. In Italy, Sisal delivered another very strong performance supported by a revamped casino experience and an expanded MyCombo product. Snai momentum also gathered pace with the product and generosity upgrades unlocked by the platform migration driving strong AMP growth. Our overall Italian online market share in Q3 grew by 2ppt year-over-year to 32% 11 making us the clear number one. Within UKI a strong performance across our portfolio of leading brands saw us take market share. Record customer engagement during the FIFA World Cup helped deliver good sportsbook handle growth while strong cross-sell helped drive double-digit iGaming revenue growth. We also recently announced the significant restructuring of our UKI business. We believe this right-sizes the UKI business going forward and positions us well to take market share in the post UK tax increase environment. While momentum in these regions was strong, our overall International revenue growth was flat year-over-year, as sports results went against us, and the impact of what has become an increasingly challenging trading environment in Brazil played through into our financial performance. Adjusted EBITDA declined by 14% primarily due to the increase in UK gaming taxes. We are very disappointed with the Government Provisional Measure banning online sports betting and iGaming in Brazil. In response, we have acted decisively; our operations are currently closed, and we have paused all discretionary and uncommitted spend. We have also restructured our business to focus on Betnacional as our sole brand in Brazil, closing our Betfair operations. The previously disclosed challenging trading environment together with the ban and the uncertain regulatory environment, resulted in a non-cash impairment of our assets in Brazil. With the right regulation, Brazil still has the opportunity to be an attractive market for us, however, we will remain disciplined in our deployment of capital as the regulatory environment continues to evolve. 4 Despite the regulatory challenges we have faced over the last 12 months, I feel very confident that our International portfolio is now well set to leverage the transformations and cost efficiencies we have delivered, continue to take market share, and deliver against our target of 5-10% annual growth. Simplifying our operating model to get more value from our scale The next phase for Flutter will be more streamlined to maximize the benefits of scale and ensure we do non-customer facing work once. That should help us move faster, reduce costs, and improve cash generation, allowing us to invest organically in the areas that drive the highest returns while also deleveraging the balance sheet. In addition to our existing International cost transformation and UK gaming tax mitigation programs, we expect to deliver an additional $500 million in gross operating cost and capital expenditure savings by 2029. By using AI, removing layers and duplication, and simplifying our technology infrastructure, we can make decisions faster, and direct greater investment towards our customers. In the US, these efficiencies will create more room to invest behind the next stage of growth. Internationally, we expect these benefits to support our previously projected long-term 5–10% annual revenue growth, while protecting adjusted EBITDA margins in more mature markets and funding investment in growth areas. Final thoughts and outlook Looking ahead, I am encouraged by the momentum we are building. My focus is on turning our progress in the US into continued delivery, and ensuring we are making the right choices to secure FanDuel’s long-term success. In International, consistent execution and further cost efficiencies should deliver continued profit growth. Flutter has an exceptional set of assets and opportunities. Realizing their full potential will require hard choices, faster decisions and strong execution. I know confidence is earned through delivery and that is what I am focused on. I look forward to sharing more on our strategy, building on the priorities I have set out today, alongside our Q4 results in February. The net loss of $1,148m for the quarter increased by $359m (Q3 2025 loss: $789m) primarily due to: • A non-cash impairment charge of $873m related to our operations in Brazil, see further detail below • A $105m increase in legal loss contingencies driven by a provision recognized in respect of a Class Action lawsuit in Australia • Lower segment profitability, with a $48m reduction in US adjusted EBITDA to $3m (-94%) and a $70m decrease in International adjusted EBITDA to $435m (-14%), as outlined below • A $45m decrease in other income, net, primarily due to a $40m year-over-year foreign exchange loss (Q3 2026 loss of $13m; Q3 2025 gain of $27m) 6 These factors were partly offset by benefits arising from: • Q3 2025 included a non-cash impairment charge of $556m relating to Junglee 13 • Q3 2025 transaction fees and associated costs included $205m related to the revision of US market access terms with Boyd Gaming Corporation • A $50m increase in income tax benefit to $95m (Q3 2025: $45m) driven by the higher year-over-year operating loss, and deferred tax benefits relating to the Brazil impairment and legal loss contingencies discussed above $537m of the post-tax Brazil impairment is allocated to the Group, reflecting the 56% ownership of Flutter Brazil. This led to a net loss attributable to Flutter shareholders of $862m for the quarter, and a loss attributable to non-controlling interests of $286m (Q3 2025: $99m). As a result, the loss per share of $4.90 was $0.99 higher year-over-year (Q3 2025: $3.91) and the adjusted loss per share of $0.18 compared with adjusted EPS of $1.64 in Q3 2025. Brazil non-cash impairment charge: The previously disclosed challenging trading environment driven by Government implemented socio-economic measures, together with the Provisional Measure issued on September 25, 2026 provisionally banning sports betting and iGaming, have resulted in Brazil revenue growth being behind expectations. Looking ahead, uncertainty remains surrounding the future operating environment. As a result, the Group has recognized total non-cash impairment charges of $873m, primarily comprising $296m related to long-lived assets and $541m related to goodwill. US Revenue grew 6% year-over-year with sportsbook revenue growth of 4% and iGaming revenue growth of 8%. Other revenue grew 20%, primarily driven by our market-making activity in the quarter. AMPs grew 12% year-over-year to 3.9m (sportsbook AMPs +9%, iGaming AMPs +24%, other AMPs +19%). Sportsbook revenue growth of 4% year-over-year driven by a strong handle performance with 13% year-over-year growth, well ahead of expectations. This was despite a headwind from sporting calendar changes year-over-year with one week less of NFL and CFB. This performance was driven by a strengthened customer proposition which included the expansion of our rewards program to all sportsbook customers and Betprotect+ expanded to NFL. New product features included improved social features such as bet-sharing, and greater personalization with our Re-Use+ and Bet it Again markets. These product improvements ensured excellent retention of players reactivated and acquired during the World Cup, with an all-time high number of customers entering the football season. We delivered growth in player frequency (+4%) and bet count (+15%) which ensured that handle growth fully offset a 60bps decline in net revenue margin to 6.8%. Net revenue margin included: • No change in structural revenue margin at 12.9% reflecting a higher proportion of MLB, which typically has a lower parlay penetration, during the quarter • No change in the impact of sports results year-over-year (Q3 2026: 10bps unfavorable, Q3 2025: 10bps unfavorable). The in-quarter net revenue impact in Q3 2026 was approximately $38m unfavorable (Q3 2025: $45m unfavorable) • A 60bps increase in promotional spend to 6.0% of handle, in-line with expectations, and reflecting our increased return of value to customers, the impact of new state launches, and investment in the FIFA World Cup. Promotional spend is expected to remain at similar levels in Q4 and for 2027, resulting in a broadly flat net revenue margin year-over-year In iGaming, exclusive new content including the launch of Huff ‘n Even More Puff Hard Hat, and content featuring Vegas Matt and Lady Luck helped deliver an increase in player frequency of 12%. These new products and features, together with our very successful launch in Alberta in July where we delivered 23% GGR share in the quarter, drove AMP growth of 24%. Revenue growth of 8% reflected a strong comparative period, which featured the launch of some of our most successful products, and the current year competitive dynamics and market moderation outlined in the shareholder letter. 7 Other revenue grew 20% driven by market-making activity. FanDuel Predicts revenue was not material during the quarter, however we made significant operational progress through our partnership with Crypto.com and the FanDuel One App delivering a step change in our product offering. New features launched since the start of the NFL season included a broader selection of sports markets, variable fees, sub-penny contracts and fractional contracts, alongside a superior promotions experience including our popular refer-a-friend mechanic. FanDuel Predicts had 66k AMPs in Q3 representing quarter-on-quarter growth of 39%, with volume of $119m and growth quarter-on-quarter of 102%. Our rapid scaling, driven by the accelerated product roadmap, translated to 271% volume growth in October when compared with July, demonstrating that our product improvements are resonating with customers. We are increasingly well-placed to capture the prediction markets opportunity and expect investment in this area to continue in 2027 at similar or higher levels given the early momentum we are delivering. Cost of sales increased by 190bps as a percentage of revenue, primarily driven by the impact of increased promotional spend and higher payment processing costs. We expect the impact of higher payment processing costs to be limited to Q3, with cost of sales as a percentage of revenue for 2026 expected to be approximately 58% and remain broadly at this level for 2027. Sales and marketing expenses were 16% higher year-over-year, driven by investment in FanDuel Predicts, our launch in Alberta and investment in the FIFA World Cup in July. Technology, research and development costs were flat year-over-year with cost savings implemented in Q2 offsetting prediction market investment and increased cloud and server costs. General and administrative costs were 6% higher year-over-year, reflecting investment in regulatory affairs and prediction markets, partially offset by the benefit of cost savings implemented in Q2. Adjusted EBITDA was $3m (Q3 2025: $51m), with a reduction in adjusted EBITDA margin of 350bps year-over-year driven by the factors detailed above. Organic iGaming revenue grew 3%, with double-digit growth in SEA and UKI offset by a decline in Brazil. International regional year-over-year revenue performance during Q3 was as follows: • UKI revenue increased 4%. iGaming revenue grew 12% driven by a 20% increase in AMPs reflecting a highly effective cross-sell strategy during the World Cup, together with new product releases including The Big Drop jackpot. Sportsbook revenue declined 6%, with strong engagement following the FIFA World Cup and the start of the new soccer season delivering a 5% increase in handle, offset by an adverse swing in sports results of 210bps. • SEA revenue increased 13%, reflecting iGaming growth of 17%, driven by strong operational execution in Italy, an expanded product offering in Türkiye and a 7-percentage point growth benefit from PokerStars’ customer migrations. Strong FIFA World Cup momentum and further product enhancements including expanding the number of MyCombo markets during the start of the new soccer season, delivered handle growth of 14%. This was offset by an adverse swing in sports results of 160bps, resulting in sportsbook revenue growth of 3%. • APAC revenue declined 4% (-10% CC), reflecting the closure of the real money gaming market in India. APAC organic revenue (Sportsbet) declined 4%, with good levels of engagement during the FIFA World Cup and closing rounds of the AFL driving handle growth of 5%, offset by an adverse swing in sports results of 60bps and an adverse sports mix. • CEE revenue grew 10%. iGaming growth of 9% reflects our continued outperformance resulting in market share gains in Georgia, Serbia and Armenia. Sportsbook revenue grew 14% reflecting strong engagement during the FIFA World Cup. We also completed the next phase of migrations onto our shared CEE technology platform, marking further progress towards unlocking a more agile operating model. • Brazil revenue declined 31% (-35% CC), impacted by the socio-economic measures implemented earlier this year and an adverse swing in sports results, offsetting the benefit of product enhancements across sportsbook and iGaming made in the quarter. We closed our operations on September 26, 2026 in accordance with the implementation of the Provisional Measure banning online betting and gaming. We are monitoring the regulatory environment closely and are ready to resume our operations once we have clarity on the future regulatory framework. • Other regions revenue was 48% lower, primarily due to a 21 percentage point growth impact from the transfer of PokerStars’ Southern European and North American customers to the SEA region and US, respectively, in addition to an overall reduction in activity on the PokerStars global platform. Adjusted EBITDA decreased by 14% year-over-year to $435m as a result of the revenue performance detailed above and a 280bps reduction in adjusted EBITDA margin to 18.0%. The reduction in margin was primarily driven by the increase in UK remote gaming duty from 21% to 40%, partially offset by the UK tax mitigation savings, and cost actions in Brazil. 9 Cost of sales as a percentage of revenue increased by 490bps to 53%, driven by the increase in UK remote gaming duty. Sales and marketing expenses decreased by 10% year-over-year reflecting lower spend in Brazil in response to the challenging trading environment. As a percentage of revenue, sales and marketing decreased by 160bps to 15.4%. Technology, research and development costs were 14% higher year-over-year driven by platform support costs relating to the PokerStars transformation program and AI software development. General and administrative costs were 10% lower reflecting savings from the UKI and PokerStars transformation programs and the India exit. Unallocated corporate overhead was flat year-over-year (-2% CC). The change in total debt from $12,266m at December 31, 2025, to $12,313m at September 30, 2026 reflects drawings of our revolving credit facility. Net debt was $10,656m at the end of Q3, with a leverage ratio of 4.6x (3.7x at December 31, 2025). We announced today that we have successfully completed the refinancing of our existing Revolving Credit Facility and Term Loan A facilities, increasing the overall facility size by approximately $240m and extending the maturity date from November 2028 to May 2032. The transaction further strengthens our debt maturity profile and provides us with further financial flexibility. We are committed to returning within our target leverage range of 2.0 - 2.5x over the medium-term consistent with our stated policy. Our immediate capital allocation priorities are to deleverage the balance sheet, while still investing in those organic growth opportunities which will deliver attractive, long-term returns. While we focus on the delivery of these capital allocation priorities, we have paused the existing share repurchase program for the foreseeable future. 2026 Guidance Early Q4 trading has been in line with expectations on an underlying basis, with unfavorable sports results in both the US and International. Our updated outlook for 2026 now includes the following: Group: Revenue of $17.61bn (+7% year-over-year) and adjusted EBITDA of $2.495bn, (-12% year-over-year) at the midpoint. 10 US: The impact of unfavorable sports results in Q3 and Q4 to date 16 . This results in reductions to revenue and adjusted EBITDA of $60m and $45m, respectively. At the midpoint, US revenue is now $7.34bn (+5% year-over-year) with adjusted EBITDA of $715m (-22% year-over-year). Guidance also reflects an improved outlook for sportsbook performance, and a reduced outlook for iGaming in light of recent trends. International: The impact of unfavorable sports results in Q3 and Q4 to date 16 (-$170m revenue and -$115m adjusted EBITDA), and the previously disclosed impact of the Brazil closure (-$70m revenue and -$20m adjusted EBITDA), which has been offset at an EBITDA level by mitigating cost actions (+$20m adjusted EBITDA). This results in reductions to revenue and adjusted EBITDA of $240m and $115m respectively. At the midpoint, International revenue is now $10.27bn (+9% year-over-year) with adjusted EBITDA of $2.09bn (-5% year-over-year). About Flutter Entertainment plc Flutter is the world’s leading online sports betting and iGaming operator, with a market leading position in the US and across the world. Our ambition is to leverage our size and our challenger mindset to change our industry for the better. By Changing the Game, we believe we can deliver long-term growth while promoting a positive, sustainable future for all our stakeholders. We are well-placed to do so through the distinctive, global advantages of the Flutter Edge, which gives our brands access to group-wide benefits, as well as our clear vision for sustainability through our Positive Impact Plan. Flutter operates a diverse portfolio of leading online sports betting and iGaming brands including FanDuel, Sky Betting & Gaming, Sportsbet, PokerStars, Paddy Power, Sisal, Snai, tombola, Betfair, MaxBet, Adjarabet and Betnacional. We are the industry leader with $16,383m of revenue globally for fiscal 2025, up 17% YoY, and $3,874m of revenue globally for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
